rows.citation: Lopes, P. H., Oliveira, B. C., Souza, A. A. de S., et al. (2022). Mitigating Computer Limitations in Replicating Numerical Simulations of a Neural Network Model With Hodgkin-Huxley-Type Neurons. Frontiers in Neuroinformatics, 16, 874234.
rows.model_type: recurrent network of 100 Hodgkin-Huxley-type neurons, implemented in C/C++, XPP/XPPAUT, Python and Matlab (RK4)
rows.controlled_mutations: partial: deliberately varied language, OS, floating-point precision and current-summation order across 72 runs; configuration variants, not single-fault mutants
rows.multiple_stimuli: no: one network scenario with fixed random applied currents; varied excitatory/inhibitory proportions rather than stimulation protocols
rows.electrophysiology_features: no: compared network mean activity and synaptic efficacy time series by absolute error exceeding 1e-4
rows.protocol_optimization: no: no test or protocol selection
rows.heldout_evaluation: no: single model; no held-out models or fault families
rows.ai_transformations: no: manual refactoring and reimplementation only
rows.software: neural-numerical-replicability2, https://github.com/wblancof/neural-numerical-replicability2 (no license detected by GitHub API)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Shows translation and numerical configuration silently change outputs of an HH network. NeuroSem would treat such changes as valid transformations or numerical mutants, with refinement-calibrated feature tolerances, multi-protocol single-cell batteries, selection and held-out evaluation.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (metadata, abstract); OpenAlex DOI record; Europe PMC full text PMC9135410 (methods: 72 scenarios, absolute-error comparison, GitHub link); GitHub REST API via gh for repository and license.

rows.citation: Iwanaga, T., Sun, X., Wang, Q., et al. (2021). Property-based Sensitivity Analysis: An approach to identify model implementation and integration errors. Environmental Modelling & Software, 139, 105013.
rows.model_type: environmental / integrated simulation models (specific models not named in abstract)
rows.controlled_mutations: unclear: abstract does not say whether errors were seeded; full text inaccessible (publisher 403, repository copy embargoed)
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial: sensitivity analysis examines many parameter configurations, not stimulation protocols
rows.electrophysiology_features: no: checks expected directions/behaviour of parameter sensitivities in environmental models
rows.protocol_optimization: no: abstract notes reuse of existing global sensitivity samples; no test selection described
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: PbSA is an oracle-free check that expected factor-effect relationships hold, without known correct outputs. NeuroSem compares transformed models to a reference under stimulation protocols with calibrated tolerances, evaluated on controlled mutants. Complementary rather than overlapping.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (metadata, no abstract); OpenAlex DOI record (closed access); Semantic Scholar DOI record (no abstract); abstract from ANU Open Research DSpace REST API item f8294068-c9f5-4212-ad81-a823712f2021 (embargoed file); ScienceDirect page returned 403.

rows.citation: Lin, X., Simon, M., Niu, N. (2021). Scientific Software Testing Goes Serverless: Creating and Invoking Metamorphic Functions. IEEE Software, 38(1), 61-67.
rows.model_type: general scientific software: EPA Storm Water Management Model (SWMM 5.1.014, C/C++)
rows.controlled_mutations: no: evaluated on real SWMM defects; no fault seeding or mutation analysis reported
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial: many metamorphic test functions derived from user forum posts vary model inputs; not stimulation protocols
rows.protocol_optimization: partial: compared invocation strategies (random, warm caches, speedy first) on runtime cost and defect detection
rows.heldout_evaluation: no: single system; no held-out models or fault families reported
rows.ai_transformations: no: NLP (NLTK, WordNet) derives relations from posts; no AI-edited code or models
rows.software: none dedicated verified; built on OpenFaaS, https://www.openfaas.com/
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Metamorphic relations and invocation scheduling for one hydrology code with real bugs. NeuroSem uses differential reference-versus-variant comparison with electrophysiology features, controlled single-fault mutants, coverage-based battery selection, cost-matched random baselines and held-out models/families.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (metadata; issue dated 2021-01); OpenAlex DOI record (short abstract; lists 2020 online year); Europe PMC ID lookup (PMC8129919); PMC author manuscript read via WebFetch summary.

rows.citation: Schölzel, C., Blesius, V., Ernst, G., et al. (2021). Countering reproducibility issues in mathematical models with software engineering techniques: A case study using a one-dimensional mathematical model of the atrioventricular node. PLOS ONE, 16(7), e0254749.
rows.model_type: one-dimensional cardiac atrioventricular-node electrophysiology model (Inada model) reimplemented in Modelica
rows.controlled_mutations: no: reports real equation, parameter and unit errors found while reproducing the model, not seeded mutants
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes: separate voltage-clamp and current-pulse experiment models reproduce several original figures and serve as tests
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial: tests compare simulation outputs with stored CSV reference data and plots; no standardized feature library noted
rows.protocol_optimization: no: tests chosen to reproduce published figures; no selection or optimization
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Applies unit tests, regression tests against reference outputs, unit checks and CI to one cardiac model. NeuroSem would measure which protocols expose silent changes, using controlled mutants, calibrated feature tolerances, battery selection and held-out evaluation.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (metadata, abstract); OpenAlex DOI record; Europe PMC full text PMC8289093 (regression tests, reference data, voltage/current-clamp experiments); GitHub REST API via gh for repository and license.
rows.found_via: Europe PMC citations of F1000 unit-testing paper

rows.citation: Parker, C., Nelson, E., Zhang, T. (2022). VeVaPy, a Python Platform for Efficient Verification and Validation of Systems Biology Models with Demonstrations Using Hypothalamic-Pituitary-Adrenal Axis Models. Entropy, 24(12), 1747.
rows.model_type: systems-biology ODE/DDE models of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis (five published models)
rows.controlled_mutations: no: no fault injection; verifies and validates existing models
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial: models compared against rest and acute stress-test (TSST) hormone data; not a stimulus battery for regression
rows.electrophysiology_features: no: ACTH and cortisol concentration time series scored with a cost function
rows.protocol_optimization: no: parameter optimization fits models to data; no test selection
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial: validation uses new, independent patient data; no held-out models for test selection
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Data-driven verification and validation of HPA axis models. NeuroSem addresses a different question: whether a transformed neuron model preserves its reference's behaviour, using stimulation batteries, controlled mutants and protocol selection.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (metadata, abstract); OpenAlex DOI record; Europe PMC full text PMC9777964 (modules, cost function, independent data, GitHub link); GitHub REST API via gh for repository and license.
